messages:
chen: Quick accessibility note from the dashboard QA: when you open the Filters flyout and navigate the virtualized tag list with VoiceOver the SR reads the chip label twice and focus sometimes lands on the flyout overlay instead of the chip. Repro: Dashboard > Filters > open > Tab into tag list > ArrowDown.
maria: thanks — do you have a short recording or console trace? Could be a duplicate aria-live announcement or a focus jump during virtualization.
chen: pasted console trace: 
```
flyout: open
virtualized-list: mount window [0..15]
aria-live: announce "Filter options loaded"
focus: set to #chip-5
aria-live: announce "Chip Label"
aria-live: announce "Chip Label"
```
jules: double announcement is usually aria-live announcing both the load message and the element being focused which also has an aria-label. If the chip itself is inside a role="list" and has aria-live or an aria-label on focus that could trigger a duplicate.
maria: good point. Do chips have aria-live? They shouldn’t. They have aria-pressed and aria-label for assistive clarity.
chen: yep, code shows `aria-label={label}` and we also slap `aria-live="polite"` on the container when loading items for NVDA compat. Maybe that's the problem.
jules: I'd remove aria-live from the container and instead put a single polite live region update like "Filters loaded, X options" and not every item. For focus falling to overlay: is overlay tabbable?
chen: the overlay has tabindex=0 so we can capture focus for escape handling. That means after virtualization settles a script moves focus into the list; but because overlay is focusable screen readers may announce it.
maria: overlay shouldn't be in the tab order. Use a FocusTrap that traps but doesn't itself require focus. For Escape handling, listen on keydown at document/body.
jules: plan suggestion: (A) remove aria-live from item container; emit a single announcement on load; (B) set overlay tabindex to -1 and avoid programmatic focus to it; (C) preserve focus when virtualization re-renders by applying data-focus-key and restore by matching key to new dom node; (D) audit chips for redundant aria-labels — prefer visible text + aria-label only when needed.
a11y-bot: Automated checks: aria-live-usage=FAIL; duplicate-announcements=2; focusable-overlay=1; contrast-issues=0; focus-visible-missing=1
chen: timeline? I can do (A) and (B) quick patch.
maria: I can own (C) with small util to map focusKey -> selector and unit test. Add a regression test that simulates virtualization reflow.
jules: I'll scan other flyouts and filters for the same pattern and update the design tokens for chip focus ring so it meets 3:1 when compact.
chen: Excellent. Also adding a short QA checklist to the ticket: 
- macOS VoiceOver: open filters > open flyout > ArrowDown through chips, verify single announcement and correct focus
- Windows NVDA: same flow
- Safari: ensure live region behaves polite (no duplicate)
- Keyboard only: Tab into filters from toolbar, open, close with Esc, focus returns to filter button
maria: putting this on RT-4589. Can we aim a small PR by Friday with tests + QA notes?
chen: yep. I'll include code comments explaining why aria-live removed for future maintainers.
a11y-bot: RT-4589 created. Priority: medium.
